scenarios.title: One Nation governs alone
scenarios.detail: Needs 45 seats. Leading in 8. Short by 37.

scenarios.title: One Nation leads a right-wing government
scenarios.detail: One Nation would need more seats than the Coalition (58) and the two together to reach 45.

scenarios.title: One Nation is kingmaker for a Coalition government
scenarios.detail: Coalition leading in 58. If it falls short of 45 but Coalition + One Nation reaches it, One Nation can demand a deal. Coalition + One Nation = 66.

scenarios.title: Coalition governs alone
scenarios.detail: Coalition leading in 58. If it reaches 45 it doesn't need One Nation in the lower house.

paths.summary: On current leads the Coalition has a majority on its own, so One Nation's influence would come through the upper house rather than the lower house.

headline.title: Coalition on track to govern alone
headline.sub: One Nation projected to win 5 seats (likely range 2 to 9). Chance it decides who governs: 0%.

seats.headline: One Nation behind after preferences
meaning: One Nation tops the first-preference vote on 37.0%, 5.5 points clear of Liberal.
To win, One Nation needs about 41.3% of the 31.4% of votes that went to other candidates to flow its way ahead of Liberal.
After preferences One Nation trails Liberal 43.7% to 56.3%.
Preferences from other candidates are flowing about 16.1% to One Nation.
Projecting that flow across every vote counted so far points to a loss (about 42.1% to One Nation after preferences).
The Greens candidate is third on 13.7%. Greens voters overwhelmingly put One Nation last, which hurts it here.
